verdict.rationale: Chroma's docs describe built-in full-text search using the $contains/$not_contains operators and regex matching with $regex/$not_regex, both usable in .get and .query alongside metadata filters. The product site also lists lexical sparse search (BM25, SPLADE), and a community user confirms built-in regex+trigram search, so no separate search engine is needed. Missing for 10: in-depth documentation of ranked BM25 lexical scoring (only a homepage bullet), and evidence that $contains goes beyond substring filtering to relevance-ranked keyword search.

support.subject: As a developer, I can run keyword/full-text search over documents inside the database without bolting on a separate search engine

citations.quote: We support full-text search with the $contains and $not_contains operators. We also support regular expression pattern matching with the $regex and $not_regex operators.
.get and .query can handle where_document search combined with metadata filtering
Sparse vector search - Lexical search (BM25, SPLADE)
Chroma has built in regex+trigram search
